html_source:
From “My Grandfather’s
Clock” (1876), an American song by
Henry C. Work, who advertised himself as one
of the Christy Minstrels. “My grandfather’s
clock was too large for the shelf, I So it stood
ninety years upon the floor; I It was taller by
half than the old man himself, I Though it
weighed not a pennyweight more. II It was
bought on the morn of the day that he was
born, / And was always his treasure and pride; /
But it stopped short, never to go again, / When
the old man died,”
